learning_outcomes.text: Know and apply nomenclature in organic and inorganic chemistry.
Identify, understand, and develop basic chemical reactions that occur in the field of industrial engineering.
Understand the properties of different states of matter and relate them to the properties of materials.
Able to perform experimental tests in the chemistry laboratory, as well as analyze, evaluate, and interpret the obtained results.
Able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Nomenclature in organic and inorganic chemistry.
Aqueous solutions: water, solubility and colligative properties.
Industrial chemistry I: hydrogen and metals.
Study of different types of chemical reactions (Lab P1).
Ebullioscopy (study of boiling point in pure liquids and solutions) (Lab P2).
Simple distillation. Density and acid-base indicators (Lab P3).
Preparation of aqueous solutions, pH measurement and neutralization (Lab P4).
Observation of a chemical equilibrium (Lab P5).
Redox titration and iron production by aluminothermy (Lab P6).
teaching_methods: Presentation of concepts and problem-solving in the classroom, and other face-to-face group sessions like discussion classes.
Personal study, report writing, practice realization as independent student work.

assessment_methods.method: Individual lab practice reports (P1, P2, P3, P4, P5-6)
Seminar 1 (SM1) - individual problem submission or activity
Seminar 2 (SM2) - individual problem submission or activity
Seminar 3 (SM3) - individual problem submission or activity
Seminar 4 (SM4) - group written work and individual presentation

assessment_rules: To pass by continuous assessment, a final grade of 5.0 or higher is required, with specific minimums for partial exams (5.0 to pass, 4.0 to apply percentage; compensable if one reaches 6.0) and the lab exam (5.0 to pass, 3.5 to apply percentage; requires 80% lab attendance). Students failing continuous assessment, or missing tests, or lacking lab attendance proceed to the Ordinary Examination. In the Ordinary Examination, only failed or missed tests are retaken, requiring a score of 5.0 or higher to pass the course. An Extraordinary Examination is a final exam covering 100% of the course, with no parts carried over, for students who fail the Ordinary Examination, also requiring a score of 5.0 or higher to pass.
